findings.element: b.css — every font-size declaration; the type ramp as a whole
findings.problem: Tracking, leading and vertical space each got a declared, named, gated ladder with a comment explaining the drift it was built to stop. Type SIZE — the axis a second product has to re-derive first — never got one. Driving all eleven states I counted 13 sizes (11, 12, 13, 15, 17, 20, 24, 30, 38, 48, 64, 96, 148) set by 71 raw px declarations, none named, none role-bound. Three of them (11, 12, 13) all carry mono micro-labels, at three different trackings (0.16em, 0.20em, 0.04em), one pixel apart, so no reader can tell 11 from 12 but any future component can pick either. That is the same drift the tracking comment says was already found and fixed on this exact object. It is also the direct answer to the round's second question: Home, Notes and Tasks cannot be built from this without copying it, because nothing here states what size a moment title is, what size a micro-label is, or what the step between them is — only what this page happened to type.
findings.fix: Add a size ladder beside the tracking and leading ladders in shell.css, named by role, and replace all 71 literals with it: --size-micro 11px (mono uppercase, the only micro-label size — retire 12px and carry the ceremonial top line on --track-labelWide instead), --size-meta 13px, --size-body 15px, --size-lead 17px, --size-title 24px, --size-head 30px, --size-hero 48px, --size-count 96px, --size-countBig 148px. Retire 20, 38 and 64 by mapping each to its neighbour (20 to --size-lead, 38 to --size-title, 64 to --size-hero). Bind each size to its leading and tracking in one class per role rather than three properties per component, and extend audit.mjs to fail any font-size that is not a token — the same check it already runs on leading.

findings.problem: The sheet measures 794 by 1440px, a ratio of 1:1.82. A4 is 1:1.414 (794 by 1123 at 96dpi). There is no @page rule, no mm, no pt, and no page-break or break-inside declaration anywhere in b.css or shell.css. So the one artifact this product makes that cannot be reflowed after it exists has no page geometry at all. Printed to A4 fit-to-page it scales to about 0.78, which puts every 11px micro-label — the rail dates, TODAY IS 16 JULY, BEHIND YOU, KEPT BY ORLA — at roughly 6.4pt and the 13px recovery line at 7.6pt, below what a grandparent reads unaided. Printed at 100 percent it runs 1.28 pages and breaks wherever the break happens to land, with nothing declaring where. Every size on this sheet is a screen size on a canvas that is not a page.
findings.fix: Give the print state real page geometry: set .b-field.b-print to width 210mm, height 297mm, padding 18mm 16mm, and add @page { size: A4; margin: 0 } plus break-inside: avoid on each moment row and on the Behind you block. Then respecify the sheet's type in points against that page rather than inheriting screen pixels: micro-label 8pt/1.4, meta 9pt, body 10.5pt, moment title 12.5pt/1.25, ceremonial date 22pt, count 96pt. Re-shoot the print frame at 794 by 1123 so the panel and the founder are looking at the object that will actually exist.

findings.element: the share link on publish, and .b-printLink on the sheet
findings.problem: The one string in this product that has to survive character by character is never once shown whole. On publish it is set white-space nowrap with overflow hidden and text-overflow ellipsis: the string renders 582px wide inside a 320px box at 390 and a 550px box at 768, 1280 and 1440, so at every viewport the owner is asked to confirm a link of which nearly half is cut, and the cut lands mid-token (…j7Qm2), which is the mid-word clamp class the defect library already paid for once. On the printed sheet the same link appears in full but at 13px, the smallest size on the page, as one unbroken 43-character case-sensitive token; a guest typing it from paper gets no grouping, no rhythm and no way to keep their place.
findings.fix: On publish, stop truncating: set the link block to font-family var(--mono), font-size 13px, line-height var(--lead-body), overflow-wrap anywhere, and let it run to two lines with the host on line one and the path on line two — a link the owner is about to send is worth 20px of height. On print, promote .b-printLink to body size (15px on screen, 10.5pt on paper), break it the same way, and set a thin space (U+2009) every four characters of the token so it can be read aloud and typed. Keep the full string in the accessible name in both places.

findings.problem: Three sentences hold a single word on their last line, and they are the three sentences doing the most emotional work on their surfaces. "…anyone holding it then sees the plan has / ended." at 14 percent of the measure, at 768, 1280 and 1440. "…and one thing that did not happen / ahead." at 19 percent, at 768, 1280 and 1440. "Saturday 8 August 2026 · in 23 / days" at 12 percent, at 390 and 1280. text-wrap balance and pretty are already used in fifteen places in b.css, so the technique is in the house — these three simply did not get it, and pretty does nothing for a two-line block in Chromium anyway. A widow on "ended." is the last word of the sentence that tells someone their link is reversible.
findings.fix: Set text-wrap: balance (not pretty) on .b-note, .b-behindNote and .b-stepRead, and give each a max-width in ch rather than px so the measure keeps its shape as the column moves: .b-note 52ch, .b-behindNote 46ch, .b-stepRead 34ch. Then put a non-breaking space before the final word of each of the three strings as a floor, since balance is not supported everywhere.

findings.problem: The leading ladder's own comment says it exists because the same object carried two baselines on the two screens it exists on. That is still true, on the newest surface. The string "Saturday 3 October 2026" is 30px at leading 1.3 on owner, desk and print, and 20px at leading 1.4 on the wedding morning — 1.4 is --lead-label, declared for mono micro-labels and single-line controls, not for the ceremonial date. A moment title is 24px at 1.3 on owner and desk, 17px at 1.3 on phone and day, and 24px at 1.2 as .b-dayNowTitle. Two kinds of object, four leadings. The gate cannot see it because audit.mjs checks that a leading is a member of the ladder, never that it is the member its role declares, so the ladder is enforced as a palette of six numbers — exactly the freedom the tracking ladder was tightened to remove. One more instance: .b-stepRead runs 15px mono at 1.5 while all nineteen other 15px mono strings run 1.4.
findings.fix: Bind leading to role in CSS instead of by hand per class: define .type-date { line-height: var(--lead-date) }, .type-title { line-height: var(--lead-head) }, .type-body { line-height: var(--lead-body) }, .type-label { line-height: var(--lead-label) }, then have .b-when and .b-dayDate compose type-date, .b-title and .b-dayNowTitle compose type-title, and .b-stepRead compose type-label. Extend audit.mjs with the check it is missing: for each declared role, assert every element carrying it renders exactly one leading across all eleven states, the same shape as the existing tracking assertion.

biggestWin: The three ladders that do exist are the real thing. Tracking, leading and vertical space are each declared once, named, commented with the drift they were built to stop, and gated — and driving all eleven states at 390, 768, 1280 and 1440 they hold: two families, two weights, no third, no rogue grey, mono used only where a figure or a label earns it, and the rail dates monospaced so the eye reads a column instead of a list. The wedding morning drawing its past in the same rail, ticks and mono dates as the future is the best typographic decision in the engagement — the past is not a different typeface, it is the same language at a smaller scale. That discipline is why this sits at 8.4 and not at 7. What stands between it and 9.5 is one build and one decision, not polish. The build is the missing size ladder: about half a day to name thirteen sizes as nine roles, replace 71 literals, and teach audit.mjs to fail an untokenised font-size and a role-mismatched leading. Until that exists, the honest answer to whether this is extractable as a named language is no — Notes and Tasks would inherit the tracking, leading and spacing ladders and then invent their own sizes, and within two products the ramp is thirteen numbers again. The decision is the printed sheet: it is a 794 by 1440 web page with a border, not an A4 page, and it has to be respecified in millimetres and points with declared page breaks before anyone prints one. The widows and the truncated share link are an hour between them.
